chapter_theme: Sahamarga (சகமார்க்கம்), the companion path, which the chapter identifies with yoga: sanmarga itself becomes sahamarga, and within yoga-samadhi are space, light and Shakti. Yoga gives the yogi both union with Siva and the enjoyments of the world; it purifies the centres and channels, cuts down the five senses with the sword of the mind, and the Lord stands within like a ripe fruit split open.
structure_note: Sanmarga as sahamarga (1488), the loss for those without the twelve-path (1489), samadhi (1490), yoga and enjoyment (1491), the purifications (1492), the five senses subdued (1493) and the ripe fruit (1494).

1488.reading: Sanmarga itself is what became sahamarga; it is the mind-path that places release within attainment; the later path is unending birth and death and the ruin of wrong-path knowledge.
1488.nuance: சகமார்க்கம் (the companion path) is in Saiva tradition the yoga path, standing with the Lord as a companion; the verse doesn't define it but joins it to sanmarga. பின்மார்க்கம் here seems to mean a fallen path, unlike 1483 where it is the lower paths. துறதி is obscure, perhaps துர்கதி (an evil end).

1489.reading: For those without the twelve-path that joins, guru, Siva and religion do not come together; fearful Lakshmi will not be in their house, and they lose form and kin together.
1489.nuance: துவாதச மார்க்கம் (the twelve-path) is unexplained; it is taken as the breath reaching the dvadasanta, twelve finger-breadths above the head, or as twelve divisions of practice. The threatened loss is worldly as well as spiritual: wealth (திருமகள்), body (உரு) and kin (கிளை).

1490.reading: Within yoga-samadhi is the wide space, within it is light, within it is Shakti; those who delight in yoga-samadhi are siddhas.
1490.nuance: அகலிடம் (the wide place) may be the world or the inner sky (ஆகாசம்); ஒளி and சத்தி are the light and power traditionally experienced there. The refrain யோகச் சமாதியின் உள்ளே makes samadhi a place one enters.

1491.reading: Both yoga and enjoyment come to yogis: those whose minds reach Siva's form through yoga have, as enjoyment, the attainment of the aims of life on earth; both belong to the yogi who does not perish.
1491.nuance: போகம் (enjoyment) is not renounced here but given to the yogi along with yoga. புருடார்த்தம் are the aims of life, traditionally dharma, wealth, pleasure and release. அழியாத யோகி may be the yogi whose body does not decay, in keeping with Tirumular's care for the body.

1492.reading: Purifying the centres and the channels, the sky-light at the end of the sixteen kalas beginning with medha, and in the abode of awareness the ordinary working of senses, instruments and intellect ceasing: this is sahamarga.
1492.nuance: ஆதாரம் (the centres, chakras), நாடி சுத்தி (cleansing the channels) and மேதாதி ஈரெண் கலை (the sixteen kalas from medha, in mantra-yoga the stages of the syllable up to the end of nada) are technical. சாதாரணம் கெடல் is read as the ordinary working of the faculties ending.

1493.reading: The five that stand rebelling he will then torment and hurl down with the sharp sword of the mind; the one the eighteen hosts contemplate has come and stood in the mind of him who can bow.
1493.nuance: The five are the senses. அயில் மன வாள் (the sharp sword of the mind) makes the mind the weapon, not the thing subdued. கணம் பதினெட்டு (the eighteen hosts) are the traditional eighteen classes of celestial beings. Who 'he' is in the first half, the yogi or the Lord, is unclear.

1494.reading: To those of rich colour he is true like a rich ripe fruit; for those whose hearts have ripened and who hold him gladly in the heart, he, the ripe fruit, splits open and stands within.
1494.nuance: The play is on கனி (fruit, to ripen): the Lord is the fruit, the devotee's heart ripens, and the fruit opens within. வளநிறத்தார் (those of rich colour) is obscure; it may be the radiant or the fortunate. பகுந்து (split open, or shared out) suggests the Lord giving himself.

links.note: 631 says samadhis are not needed for one who goes with the Lord and there is no samadhi once one becomes Him; 1490 praises yoga-samadhi as holding space, light and Shakti. Samadhi is honoured as a means and set below union.

Both arm the mind against the five senses: the Kural's goad of firmness guards them like elephants, Tirumular's sharp sword of the mind cuts them down. The Kural guides the five; Tirumular strikes them.

Tirumanthiram 1489 says that for those without the joining path the fearful Lakshmi will not be in their house (வெருவுந் திருமகள் வீட்டில்லை). Kural 167 says the fair goddess (செய்யவள்), grudging the envious man, shows him to her elder sister. Both use the figure of Lakshmi leaving a house as the mark of failure, the Kural for envy, Tirumular for lacking the yogic path; 1489's reading is uncertain.

Tirumanthiram 274 tells the reader to melt in love (அன்புருக்கி) and seek the First One, and Nandi's love then stands foremost. Tirumanthiram 1494 says that for those whose hearts have ripened (உளங்கனிந்து), he, the ripe fruit, splits open and stands within (பழங்கனிந்து உள்ளே பகுந்துநின்றானே). 1494 turns 274's melting into ripening, and has the Lord ripen in answer.

source_issues: 1492 line 4 reads சாதா ரணங்கெட லாஞ்ச மார்க்கமே; ஆஞ்ச மார்க்கம் is probably ஆம் சகமார்க்கம், with a syllable lost.
1488: துறதி is obscure and may be corrupt.
